target_customer: Startups and enterprises hiring tech talent, mainly in India and for remote roles
problem: Founders struggled to source engineers through conventional channels; the founders spent about three months hiring their first engineer at their previous startup.
business_model: contingency recruiting fee (15 percent of annual salary per the site) plus marketplace subscriptions with outreach credits
product_category: AI recruiting and outbound candidate sourcing

founders.name: Amit Singh
founders.background_notes: YC page says he built and exited Memer. The Weekday story page says the founders ran Memer and sold it to ShareChat.

founders.name: Anubhav Malik
founders.background_notes: YC page says he built technology at Unacademy, ShareChat and Memer.

competitors.name: Hirect
competitors.what: Chat-based direct hiring app connecting job seekers with founders and HR leads in India
competitors.traction_then: Began operating mid 2020; recruiters paid Rs 199 per hot listing in 2021

competitors.name: Instahyre
competitors.what: Employer-paid AI matching platform for tech hiring in India
competitors.traction_then: Operating before the batch; the dated source is later
competitors.funding_then: About 540K USD seed per a Crunchbase-based analysis, unverified

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a large contact database and outreach tooling is data and operations heavy but standard engineering for a small team; the later AI sourcing agent adds modeling work.

defensibility.rationale: The claimed database of 250 million profiles is a partial moat but recruiting data sources and outreach tools are widely available and the site itself contrasts with many agencies and sourcing tools.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent acquisition or copy was found in sources; Weekday kept growing and by its own report reached 600 plus customers.

market_need_then: The founders' own experience of a roughly three month search for a first engineer, as told on the Weekday story page. No dated external demand data found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and confident with stated values such as no bullshit, pro-active and urgency; some copy is bold and some pages show unfinished placeholder text.

branding.community_and_virality: Runs a blog, podcast and newsletter and candidate tools such as resume scorers and salary calculators, per the site.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic common word name, no brand press found; tone and free candidate tools help acquisition but no source shows brand pull.

pivots.from: Reference based hiring network where engineers refer talent from their social graph, as described in 2023 coverage
pivots.to: AI recruiter that runs outbound sourcing campaigns (current positioning)
pivots.why: Not stated by a source; the positioning changed between 2023 coverage and the current YC and site descriptions.

outcome_analysis: Weekday is a Bengaluru recruiting company founded by a team that had just sold Memer to ShareChat and felt the hiring pain directly. After the Winter 2021 batch it raised a 2.2M USD seed in August 2023 and by its own reports reached seven-figure revenue and 600 plus customers, though those figures are company-reported. Its positioning moved from referrals to AI outbound sourcing, and no shutdown, acquisition or layoffs were found.
notes: Seed amount and lead stated by Entrackr, Entrepreneur India and People Matters. Sources differ slightly on totals (2.2 to 2.46M USD). General Catalyst backing appeared on one weak source and is unverified. The site links press headlines suggesting 22 million USD in 2023, which conflicts with the 2.2M USD outlets and is treated as a typo in those links. Company-reported figures (600 customers, seven-figure revenue) are unverified. Education not found for any founder. Instahyre is dated by a 2022 article though it existed earlier. The outcome search found no layoffs, acquisition or shutdown for Weekday.
